title: Crash-Safe Coordination: Monotonic Lease Fencing, Idempotent Transitions, and State Recovery for the Multi-Agent Flight Board
target_platform: Local deterministic subprocesses and fault-injection harness; manage_coordination.py; board.json; leases.jsonl
hypothesis: Extending the existing flight board with monotonic lease generations, idempotent transition identifiers, and recoverable state updates will produce zero accepted stale-owner operations, zero simultaneous valid overlapping leases, and zero lost acknowledged handoffs across 1,000 fault-injected schedules, while recovery completes within 5 seconds p95 and normal coordination latency overhead increases by <= 20%.
falsification_criteria: Any stale lease holder can renew, release, or publish through coordination-managed operations after reassignment; any schedule grants overlapping valid leases; an acknowledged handoff disappears after recovery; replay produces duplicate logical transitions; or recovery or latency targets fail. (A lease token does not prevent direct arbitrary filesystem writes by an uncooperative process; the scope protects coordination-managed operations and publication checks).
experiment: Use disposable Git repositories and controlled processes to inject failures: (1) two simultaneous checkout attempts for overlapping targets, (2) process termination between journal and board updates, (3) lease expiry, reassignment, then delayed heartbeat/checkin from original owner, (4) duplicate checkins and interrupted handoff persistence, (5) clock changes and malformed trailing journal records. Test existing implementation first; add only mechanisms demonstrated necessary by failures.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: Escalate to bounded standard review solely for mathematical or formal proof of concurrency invariants.

related_missions.MISSION-008: PROVIDER of durable handoff storage; distinct from testing whether checkpoint content improves agent comprehension.
